summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 在扑克等隐藏信息游戏中，由于规模巨大，通常采用离线计算蓝图策略并在实时对局中进行子博弈求解来优化。在二人零和博弈中，这种求解方式已被证明是安全的，即不会增加被对手剥削的风险。但在三人及以上独立决策的多人博弈中，缺乏类似的安全性保证，启发式求解可能导致策略漏洞被利用。本文正是针对这一理论空白，提出首个适用于非相关多方配置的安全子博弈求解后验证书。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 模型考虑一个n人不完美信息扩展式博弈，其中一名玩家（求解者）在达到某个公共状态后，对其子博弈内的策略进行更新，其余玩家保持蓝图策略不变。安全性通过‘最佳响应差距’（best-response gap）衡量，即任一玩家单方面偏离当前策略所能获得的最大收益。论文定义了四个可计算量：蓝图未兑现的价值承诺、求解误差、对手在子博弈中的最佳响应收益超出预期的部分，以及总效用变化的结构性税项。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文证明了一个条件安全定理：任何子博弈更新所导致的最佳响应差距上升，至多等于上述四项之和。这四项分别捕捉了因求解者兑现潜在价值、求解不精确、对手间价值转移及总效用变化带来的风险。该定理为任意更新提供了后验安全证书，并在常数和博弈（如无抽水扑克）中，结构性税项为零，从而实现了紧致边界。实验证明该证书能有效过滤有害更新。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 证明分为两步：首先在总效用恒定情形下，利用对手策略分解与完美回忆性质，结合子博弈内最佳响应分析，建立各玩家收益变化与证书项的关系；随后通过转移引理，将一般情形的总效用漂移控制在结构性税项内。关键技术在于将对手的子博弈外行为与内部最佳响应分离，并通过反事实权重精确量化偏差。最终界限由一次子博弈内每个对手的最佳响应计算即可验证。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 该结果仅适用于单次全深度子博弈更新，无法直接推广到带叶节点估值的有限深度求解。此外，证书虽能检测风险，但不提供自动修复机制。尽管如此，本文首次为多人博弈中的实时策略改进提供了理论安全保障，其证书机制可直接集成于Pluribus类系统。最值得阅读的是其清晰的问题抽象、紧致的四项分解结构及其在真实扑克环境下的有效性验证。

paper.title: Pareto-Optimal and Strategyproof Data-Sharing Between Competitors

rawOutput.titleZh: 竞争者之间的帕累托最优与策略证明数据共享

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 为什么竞争对手之间会愿意共享数据？传统观点认为，企业因担心提升对手竞争力而不愿分享数据。本文指出，在基于预测质量竞争的市场中，企业利润由市场份额和模型精度共同决定：共享数据虽可能削弱相对优势，但能普遍提升模型性能。作者探究是否存在一种机制，能让所有企业在共享后均受益，并解决企业虚报自身数据量的激励问题。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 模型考虑多个竞争企业在同一市场运营，每个企业拥有一定规模的数据集。客户选择行为分为两阶段：首先根据各企业模型精度的概率选择访问哪家公司（市场份额），然后根据推荐质量决定是否成交（精度）。企业的最终收益是两者乘积。数据共享通过合同规定各方交换的数据比例，允许非对称和部分共享，最终数据量影响所有企业的市场表现。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文证明，帕累托最优的数据共享合同总是使至少一家企业获得全部数据。更进一步，作者提出一类‘等增益’共享合同，确保所有企业从共享中获得相同比例的利润增长，并保持相对市场份额不变。其中特定合同不仅满足帕累托最优，还具备策略证明性——即使企业试图低报自身数据量也无法获利，尤其在数据量较大时欺骗收益趋近于零。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者通过构造参数化的等增益合同族来平衡企业间的利益分配。利用精确函数的凹性假设，结合中间值定理与不等式放缩，证明该机制下企业无法通过谎报初始数据量获益。对于离散情况，通过上下界分析展示舍入误差对策略稳定性的影响极小。整个分析依赖于市场占有率公式的结构特性与效用函数的单调性关系。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 模型假设所有企业使用相同精度函数且仅以数据量区分，忽略了数据质量差异与异构模型能力。实证结果显示经验精度函数未必严格凹，但在宏观层面仍近似成立。尽管如此，核心机制在真实数据上表现稳健。最值得阅读的是其机制设计理念与策略证明性的构造方式，为竞争环境下的合作提供了可操作的理论方案。

paper.title: Closing Gaps in Temporal Fair Division for Chores

rawOutput.titleZh: Closing Gaps in Temporal Fair Division for Chores

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 论文探讨在任务按顺序到达且不可更改分配的情况下，如何公平地分派不可分割的家务任务（chore）。传统公平性如无嫉妒性（envy-freeness）在动态场景下难以满足，即使已知全部任务序列，仅因无法回溯调整，也可能导致公平性崩溃。作者关注时间维度下的公平性（temporal fairness），特别是是否存在始终满足某种公平标准的分配方式，这是当前研究中的开放问题。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 模型设定为一组代理（agents）依次接收到来的任务（chores），每个任务必须在到达时立即分配且不可撤销。代理的成本函数为加性，公平性要求在每个前缀分配后都满足“至多差一个任务的无嫉妒性”（TEF1）。研究聚焦于是否存在满足该条件的分配，以及其计算复杂性，特别区分了任务为商品（goods）与家务（chores）的不同情况。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文证明了对于至少三个代理，TEF1分配不一定存在，并且判断其存在性是NP完全问题，即使所有成本非常接近。此外，最优的时间公平因子可能无界，意味着任何固定放松都无法保证存在。同时，即使存在TEF1分配，最小化社会成本也是难以近似的。这些结果解决了Elkind等人提出的公开问题。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者通过构造特定实例来证明非存在性和复杂性下界，例如利用几何增长的成本向量制造不可避免的公平性破坏。对于正向结果，设计了一个全多项式时间近似方案（FPTAS），用于逼近最优时间EF1因子，并保证社会成本不高于达到该因子的最便宜分配。关键技术是基于几何区间对状态进行分组的动态规划。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 论文的负向结果依赖于精心构造的成本结构，现实中可能较少出现。虽然FPTAS提供了实用近似，但它放松了精确公平性。然而，论文清晰揭示了时间公平性的根本难度，特别是在三个以上代理时的质变。最值得阅读的是其对TEF1存在性与复杂性的完整刻画，以及巧妙的构造性证明和近似算法设计。

paper.title: Sequential Contract Design for Budgeted Crowdsourcing

rawOutput.titleZh: 预算受限众包中的序贯合约设计

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 为什么不能直接按成果付费？因为工人努力不可见，只能通过结果间接激励，而结果随机导致支付也随机，但总预算必须硬性不超支。这使得一个工人的激励合同会影响后续可用资金，形成强耦合。本文研究在固定预算下如何动态设计合约序列，在观测到前序结果后决定下一个工人及合同，以最大化期望产出。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 模型中有多个工人，每人有多档努力水平和多种可能结果，努力影响结果分布但不可见。委托人依次接触工人，基于剩余预算和历史结果提供合约（即各结果对应的付款）。工人选择使自身收益最大化的努力水平，委托人目标是最大化总期望价值，同时确保任何结果路径下的累计支付不超过预算，即满足事后预算约束。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文刻画了最优自适应策略的近似可能性：当工人数、每人的努力档数或结果种类任一为常数时，存在多项式时间常数因子近似算法；但三者均无界时，除非P=NP，否则不存在常数因子近似。此外，对风险自由行代理人和单调子模估值等情形也获得了紧的近似保证。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 核心方法是构建线性规划松弛，结合预算阈值离散化与刚性合约族，并利用对偶和椭球法处理指数级变量。关键技术包括通过随机舍入实现可行性，利用子模极大化或随机探测框架处理非加性估值，以及针对特定结构（如相同代理人）设计动态规划与舍入方案来逼近最优解。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 主要局限在于许多正向结果依赖于参数为常数的假设，且简单局部合约在一般情况下表现极差。尽管如此，论文的价值在于清晰揭示了预算约束、隐藏行动与序贯决策三者的交互复杂性，其LP+舍入框架和对适应性的分析对相关领域有较强借鉴意义，值得细读其模型抽象与主定理证明。

fetchedPapers.title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
fetchedPapers.abstract: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. In this paper, we present ROGUE-AI (Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation), a multi-agent framework that closes the above gap and rebuilds each reported incident offline together with a matched control that lacks only the blamed cause, and runs agents on both. Our results suggest that ROGUE-AI is able to reproduce the reported harm in 89% of its 108 attempted replications. Agents built on five current GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models made the reported mistake in 18% to 33% of runs, against at most 1% without the blamed cause. Of the 72 incidents with real-world harm, 62 had no underlying attacker, and in these, agents did what their task asked for but missed an ordinary hazard, such as a database shared with the live site. Replications without an attacker caused more harm than replications of prompt injection for all five models. Defenses against prompt injection look for injected instructions, but these replications contain none. Further, a warning after each tool output that names the hazard and its consequence lowered harm for all five models, whereas a note of the same length that does not mention the hazard left most of the harm in place. Built from real incidents, the ROGUE-AI replications form a reusable audit framework that vendors can rerun before each new release.

fetchedPapers.title: Public-Private Cooperation in the Port of Rotterdam: An Agent-Based Toy Model of Cooperative Efforts Against Cocaine Trafficking
fetchedPapers.abstract: Cocaine trafficking poses a persistent governance challenge in the Port of Rotterdam (PoR), requiring cooperation between public and private actors. This paper develops an Agent-Based toy Model (ABM) coupled with a Causal Loop Diagram (CLD) to explore interactions between trust, cooperation, competition, pressure, enforcement, and actor skills in public-private cooperation (PPC). Based on empirical data of PPC in the PoR, we explore responses to parameter shocks across different initial configurations. In this model, effectiveness of PPC is strongly state-dependent and measures institutional, relational, behavioral, and resource readiness. The toy model demonstrates that isolated, single-track measures yield limited long-term gains modelled over 5 years due to structural system inertia, whereas coordinated multi-parameter strategies produce substantial improvements. Specifically, combining trust-building, cooperation, and moderate pressure with reduced regulatory enforcement friction raises effectiveness by 25% from a baseline effectiveness, compared to just 13% for an isolated increase in cooperation. Acknowledging the exploratory nature of the model, these findings offer exploratory hypotheses on port security governance. Future work should validate the model against test cases and additional expert input.

fetchedPapers.title: Law at the Speed of AI: Critical Legal Infrastructure for the Machine Age: Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA)
fetchedPapers.abstract: The global deployment of autonomous AI agents within and across organisations exceeds the governance infrastructure available to constrain it. Agent communication and authentication protocols, principally the Model Context Protocol and the Agent2Agent Protocol, are maturing quickly, but maturity at the protocol layer does not produce legal legibility at the governance layer. Runtime enforcement written by the deploying organisation fixes the resources an AI agent can reach, not the authority under which it acts. Legal legibility is the capacity of a legal system to recognise, interpret and regulate activity by mapping it onto legal personhood, property, rights and liabilities. Existing (analogue) legal infrastructure cannot supply it for autonomous deployment. The resulting deficit is bidirectional. It concerns the attribution of liability when an AI agent causes harm, and the allocation of rights, including data and economic rights, generated by agentic activity and by the AI agent itself as a source of value and form of property. This paper characterises that deficit as the legal attribution gap, a material and unaddressed risk to economies, organisations and citizens that is magnified in cross-organisational multi-agent deployment. The paper describes the Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA), in which AI systems and data assets are registered as legal objects anchored to one or more identified legal persons, governed by cryptographically tethered smart legal instruments and evaluated at runtime. Each smart legal instrument can carry a legal context clause, through which the legislation, regulation and judicial decisions in force at the time of the act are given practical and legal effect in that evaluation. Infrastructure of this kind is a precondition for the continued function of any legal, property and economic system with both human and autonomous machine stakeholders.

fetchedPapers.title: Evolving Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction
fetchedPapers.abstract: Quantum computation entails robustness engineering: a noisy quantum state is measured continuously, and a classical algorithm (the decoder) must infer corrections that reliably remove the noise, fast enough to keep up. We write several published belief-propagation (BP) decoders for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes in a Domain-Specific Language (DSL), and search over it with grammatical evolution. Written in the language, the published decoders show their parameters in plain view, allowing us to re-parameterise BP+OSD (ordered statistics decoding) and BP+LSD (localized statistics decoding) decoders with damping, before any search, making each 17.1--41.0$\times$ faster at a higher error rate, and BP+OSD-0 about 103 faster than the ldpc package's version tuned on the [[72,12,6]] bivariate-bicycle code. Evolution over the language finds decoders that improve the time-error front. One makes 23% fewer logical errors than BP+OSD-0 with damping at 0.64$\times$ its time, and decoders evolved from random code are more accurate than ldpc's tuned BP+OSD-0 at 1/31 of its time or less. Frozen at one operating point, the two fastest evolved decoders generalize well across noise levels, code sizes and round counts, staying at the time-error front. Ultimately, we demonstrate that capturing expert knowledge within a DSL creates a powerful intermediate layer---one that effectively bridges human intuition and machine-driven optimization to unlock highly efficient quantum error correction.

fetchedPapers.title: Coherent belief and opinion propagation produces more echo chambers: corrected version
fetchedPapers.abstract: The occurrence of echo chambers is a well-known phenomenon in social networks. Echo chambers are groups of agents satisfying three properties: homogeneity, i.e., sharing the same opinion, segregation, i.e., listening primarily to agents of the same group, and reinforcement, i.e., increasing opinion similarity over time. Opinion dynamics models have been used to explain how echo chambers occur through agents updating their opinions. However, social network users also exchange beliefs supporting their opinions. Here, we aim at identifying the effect of propagating beliefs together with opinions on the formation of echo chambers. For that purpose, we complement an existing opinion dynamics model with classical belief merge operations. Beliefs and opinions are also maintained coherent guided by values that agents share. We introduce measures, applying to either beliefs and opinions, to identify echo chambers based on the three properties. This model is used to simulate opinion and belief propagation with varying initial conditions and agent tolerance for different opinions/beliefs. Results confirm the occurrence of echo chambers observed in previous opinion dynamics studies in a different setting and with a stricter measure. They also demonstrate the occurrence of echo chambers with belief propagation. Finally, they show that connecting opinions to beliefs and maintaining their coherence increases the number of belief echo chambers, but that they involve a reduced number of agents.

fetchedPapers.title: Interlacing Committees with Edge-Expansion
fetchedPapers.abstract: Approval-based committee selection has recently been studied through the lens of \emph{interlacing}, a framework for studying polarization in approval elections, in which committees induce a similarity graph over voters. The quality of committees is then evaluated through the connectivity of the resulting graph. We revisit the connectivity measures used in this framework and propose \emph{edge-expansion}, a classical graph-theoretic measure with well-established connections to polarization in networks, as the optimization objective. We provide a theoretical foundation for this proposal by relating interlacing to classical models of information diffusion and by comparing edge-expansion with previously proposed connectivity objectives, identifying qualitative differences in the structural properties they capture. Finally, we study the computational complexity of optimizing edge-expansion, showing that hardness persists even for voter-interval preferences, while the problem is polynomial-time solvable for every fixed committee size, with an improved dependence on the committee size for voter-candidate-interval preferences.

fetchedPapers.title: DS2Agent: Holistic Device Agents for Accelerated Embedded Board-Level Design
fetchedPapers.abstract: Embedded board-level development demands extensive expertise, from component selection and device characteristics to interface configuration, driver writing, and system composition. Recently, LLM-based agents have shown strong capabilities, raising the prospect of automating board-level design tasks. However, existing agents either target chip-level design or treat datasheets as static text, offering little guidance on whether a specific component should---or even could---be used for a given board-level design. Moreover, without touching real hardware, they hallucinate incorrect details. To fill this gap, we present {\setlength{\fboxsep}{1pt}\href{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DS2Agent-9FE8/}{\fcolorbox{blue}{white}{DS2Agent}}}, an open-source framework that constructs interactive agents from device datasheets. Each agent comprises three models: a knowledge model supporting retrieval and question answering; a digital-twin model capturing the physical functionality of the device; and an interface model supporting driver development and system integration. To suppress hallucinations, we also allow optional connections to real devices, so that the agent can calibrate its internalized knowledge against the device. We evaluate DS2Agent on ten devices spanning seven functional categories. Compared with the baseline, the DS2Agent-augmented agent improves the question-answering score from 87 to 97 out of 100 while using 44.8\% fewer tokens. For driver generation, it reduces average token usage per device by 72.9\%. For system integration, it reduces total token usage across three FreeRTOS applications by 29.7\%.

fetchedPapers.title: GRODE-RTL: Source-Mapped Dependency Views for LLM-Based RTL Repair
fetchedPapers.abstract: Large Language Models show great potential for automated Register-Transfer Level repair, yet they struggle with non-local faults where root causes and failing outputs reside far apart in source code. Treating RTL as a flat token sequence obscures hardware dataflows, whereas exposing complete synthesized graphs overwhelms the model with fine-grained metadata. To resolve this representation dilemma, we propose GRODE-RTL, an anchor-centric representation that extracts the single-clock-stage fan-in cone of a suspect register from the netlist, maps netlist nodes back to editable source lines, and organizes them into a compact hop-partitioned dependency view. By prioritizing direct drivers and folding distant hops, GRODE-RTL guides standard tool-using agents without exposing ground-truth hints or oracle feedback. We evaluate GRODE-RTL across 30 formally validated non-local faults using three LLMs (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.2, and MiniMax-M3) alongside a controlled six-configuration ablation study. GRODE-RTL improves pass@1 over source-level exploration by 16.7% on DeepSeek, by 26.7% on GLM-5.2, and by 20.0% on MiniMax-M3, with consistent gains on the hard-to-retrieve far-distance and indirect-anchor subsets of all three models. Our controls isolate structural relevance from generic context expansion, proving that selective dependency organization rather than full graph exposure is key to effective RTL repair.

summarySections.modelAndSetup: 研究聚焦于[[72,12,6]]双变量自行车码在电路级噪声下的解码任务，输入为多轮综合征序列，输出为逻辑错误率。作者构建了一个领域特定语言（DSL），将BP类解码器表达为可演化的程序，并采用语法进化结合MAP-Elites算法进行搜索。评估基于真实物理模拟数据，以解码时间与逻辑错误率的帕累托前沿作为核心指标。

paper.title: Law at the Speed of AI: Critical Legal Infrastructure for the Machine Age: Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA)

rawOutput.titleZh: AI时代的法律基础设施：法律之下的自主性架构（AULA）

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 随着自主AI代理在全球组织间广泛部署，现有法律体系难以跟上其运行速度，导致责任归属模糊、权利分配不清。当前技术协议虽能确保通信与认证，却无法提供法律上的可解释性。这种‘法律归因鸿沟’使得AI造成损害时难以追责，也阻碍了数据与经济权利的合法界定，尤其在跨组织多代理环境中风险被进一步放大。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 论文提出Autonomy Under Law Architecture（AULA），将AI系统和数据资产注册为锚定于特定法律主体的‘法律对象’。通过两个开源协议LARC和AURA，AULA在运行时记录AI活动并验证其授权来源。系统结合数字身份、智能法律工具（SLI）和加密机制，在技术执行层与法律规范之间建立映射，使AI行为具备法律上下文，从而支持司法追溯与合规审计。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: AULA首次系统性地将法律人格、财产权和责任机制嵌入AI代理架构中，填补了技术能力与法律问责之间的结构性空白。它不仅为政府和企业提供可审计的责任闭环，还支持保险与风险管理机制的落地。模拟实验正在超级计算设施中进行，初步成果显示采用AULA可显著降低AI部署带来的社会与经济风险。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: AULA通过绑定AI代理与其背后的法律主体，利用智能法律工具预设权限边界，并借助LARC实现公开匿名交易记录、AURA实现在组织间动态验证代理权限。该架构不取代现有法律流程，而是作为中间层与法院、监管机构互操作，使自动化决策能在法律框架内被执行与追溯，从而实现‘机器速度的法治’。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: AULA的效果依赖于参与方注册比例，低覆盖率会削弱整体防护能力。目前尚未完全解决非注册系统的互操作问题，也未涵盖所有司法管辖区的法律差异。最值得阅读的是其对法律归因鸿沟的定义、AULA机制设计细节及与现实法律制度的衔接路径，这对构建可信AI生态系统具有指导意义。

rawOutput.titleZh: 基于边扩展的交织委员会

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 现有批准制委员会选举模型通过选民间的共同认可关系构建连接图，并以直接连接数（PAIRS）或可达性（CONS）衡量委员会质量。但前者忽视全局连通，后者无法区分脆弱桥接与强连接结构，难以反映社会凝聚力与极化的本质差异。本文指出，仅靠连接存在与否不足以评估委员会对社会分裂的缓解能力，需更精细的结构性指标。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 论文将委员会诱导的选民图视为社会互动网络，提出以图论中的边扩展（CHGR，即切图常数）作为优化目标，量化不同群体间连接的稳健性。输入为选民对候选人的批准投票，输出为k人委员会。目标是最大化诱导图的边扩展值，从而选出能最有效地弥合社会分歧、促进共识形成的委员会，其性能通过CHGR得分与其他目标对比评估。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文证明边扩展能显著细化传统目标：两个在CONS下表现相同的连接委员会，其CHGR得分差距可达二次方因子，揭示了前者无法捕捉的结构性弱点。在特定偏好域下，该差距仍保持线性。信息扩散模型进一步佐证，高CHGR值意味着更快的共识达成速度，为该指标提供了动态行为层面的合理性，强化了其作为极化治理工具的价值。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者将边扩展引入委员会选举框架，建立了其与信息共识时间的理论联系。通过构造反例，揭示了PAIRS和CONS目标的结构性缺陷。计算上，证明了即使在限制性偏好域（VI）下，精确求解CHGR最优委员会仍是NP难问题。但针对固定委员会大小k，提出了基于选民类型的多项式时间算法，并利用VCI偏好结构改进了算法复杂度。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 核心局限在于CHGR本身不区分不同的非连通图（均为零分），且最优委员会的计算复杂度高，尤其在一般偏好下。尽管如此，论文的价值在于深刻揭示了现有评估标准的不足，并为委员会设计提供了兼具理论深度与现实意义的新视角。最值得阅读的是其对极化与连通性的结构性分析，以及信息扩散模型提供的第二层论证逻辑。
